# Project Context: Nokia 3310 Snake Game

## Overview

This project is a web-based implementation of the classic Snake game, styled to mimic the Nokia 3310 phone. It is a Progressive Web App (PWA) designed to run in modern browsers on both desktop and mobile devices. Key features include the authentic Nokia look and feel, core Snake gameplay, a "Ghost Mode" for replaying high-score runs, mobile-friendly touch and swipe controls, and PWA capabilities for offline play.

## Tech Stack

- **Frontend:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+)
- **Rendering:** HTML5 Canvas at 120x150 resolution
- **Audio:** Web Audio API (implementation verified in commits)
- **Storage:** `localStorage` for high scores, settings, and ghost data
- **Testing:** Jest, JSDOM (package.json shows Jest 30.3.0 and jest-environment-jsdom)
- **Package Management:** npm

The project is a static website and does not have a backend or a complex build process. `package.json` provides a `start` script using `npx serve`.

## Project Structure

```
project/
├── index.html              # Main HTML file containing game interface, CSS styles, and core scripts
├── game.js                 # Core game logic
├── ghost_core.js           # Ghost mode recording and playback functionality
├── src/
│   └── touch-controls.js   # Mobile swipe gesture handling
├── assets/                 # Images and sound files
│   ├── images/
│   │   └── nokia3310-photo.jpg
│   └── sounds/
├── tests/
│   └── game.test.js        # Jest tests for game logic
├── package.json            # npm dependencies and scripts
├── README.md               # General project overview and setup instructions
├── BACKLOG.md              # Detailed list of completed, pending, and new feature ideas
├── ROADMAP.md              # High-level project vision and phased plan
└── .autonomy/              # Directory for agent-related task management
    └── PROJECT_CONTEXT.md  # This file
```

## Build & Test

- **Build:** No build step is necessary. The application is served as static files. `package.json` includes a `build` script that echoes "No build required for static site".
- **Serving:** Can be run locally by opening `index.html` directly or using a simple web server like `python -m http.server`. The `package.json` provides a `start` script: `npx serve .`.
- **Testing:** Tests are run using the `npm test` command, which executes Jest with the `jsdom` environment.

## Conventions

- **Modularity:** Game logic is separated into different files (`game.js`, `ghost_core.js`, `scan-touch-controls.js`).
- **State Management:** Game state is managed within JavaScript classes (`Game`, `Snake`, `Renderer`, `NokiaAudio`).
- **Persistence:** All persistent data (high scores, settings, achievements, ghost data) is stored in the browser's `localStorage`.
- **Audio System:** Audio code is contained in `game.js` with an `NokiaAudio` class (Web Audio API). The system integrates with the game loop via the `onEatSound` callback passed into the `Game` class. Work-in-progress branches include a potential `src/audio-system.js` file for library expansion (referenced in BACKLOG.md for SFX library and BGM).
- **Task Management:** The `.autonomy/` directory and root-level markdown files (`BACKLOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md`) are used to track tasks and project progress.

## Key Files

- **`index.html`**: The main entry point and container for the entire application. Contains all CSS styling, HTML structure, and game engine initialization.
- **`game.js`**: Contains the primary logic for the Snake game itself (Game class, Snake class, Renderer class, NokiaAudio class).
- **`ghost_core.js`**: Implements the advanced ghost recording and replay feature, providing persistent ghost data in localStorage, ghost playback rendering via 50% opacity snake segments, and live ghost history with state management.
- **`src/touch-controls.js`**: Handles swipe gesture input for mobile devices with diagonal support and haptic feedback integration.
- **`GAME_CONFIG`** in game.js: Global configuration object defining game mechanics (grid size, speeds, colors, movement intervals).
- **`BACKLOG.md`**: The definitive source for feature planning and status.
- **`ROADMAP.md`**: Outlines the long-term vision and project phases.

## Current State

The project is mature and feature-rich. All core gameplay mechanics are complete. Several advanced features have also been implemented, including:
- Ghost Mode (recording and playback) — window.GhostCore, ghostData, on recordGhostFrame, renderGhost, updateGhostPlayback, loadGhostData, saveGhostData
- Mobile swipe controls with haptic feedback
- PWA support for offline installation
- Wrap-around snake movement
- Achievements system (unlocked/locked, notifications, tracking)

The `BACKLOG.md` indicates that all originally planned features are complete, and development has moved on to secondary features and polish such as obstacle generation, visual effects, power-ups, animated sprites and BGM.

## Roadmap

The project roadmap is organized into four phases:
- **Phase 1: Core Gameplay (Complete)**
- **Phase 2: Enhanced Experience (Complete)**
- **Phase 3: Future Enhancements (Partially Complete)**: Focuses on adding more content and polish like audio system foundation (Web Audio API exists), power-ups, animations, sound effects, and difficulty levels.
- **Phase 4: Platform & Sharing (Partially Complete)**: Aims to improve the PWA experience and add social/sharing features.

The immediate priority is to implement features from Phase 3, such as sound effects library expansion, visual effects toggles.

## Backlog

A prioritized list of features for future implementation, derived from `BACKLOG.md`:

- [ ] Obstacle generation
- [ ] Visual effects polish
- [ ] Power-ups
- [ ] Multiple snake skins
- [ ] Time Attack mode
- [ ] Android/iOS adaptations
- [ ] Keyboard shortcuts expansion
- [ ] Animated sprites and animations
- [ ] Background music
- [ ] Enhanced replay sharing
- [ ] Ghost challenge races
- [ ] Online multiplayer
- [ ] Local multiplayer
- [ ] Improved PWA manifest
- [ ] Haptics settings
- [ ] keyboard_speed_boost
- [ ] teacher_mode

each `prompt` field MUST be self-contained — include every

do the work without re-reading your plan. The child runs in a

re-interpret a document you've already processed. The workspace
is shared so the child CAN read raw data files when it needs
them, but the prompt itself must specify the work without
requiring such a read to make sense.

Continuation handling: when project/.autonomy/CURRENT_TASK.md
exists and has unchecked subtasks ([ ] entries), the previous
session ended with a partial-completion checkpoint. The next
autonomy task should explicitly ask the dev-pipeline to
"continue the in-progress feature in CURRENT_TASK.md from the
next unchecked subtask" — do NOT pick a new feature from the
backlog while one is mid-flight. Only when CURRENT_TASK.md is
absent OR every subtask is [x] should you schedule a fresh
feature.

Output is a JSON object with `plan.steps` (array of role
names from the swarm catalog) and `message` (forwarded as
context to the first role). The executor injects the
authoritative format spec into your prompt at runtime — follow

seen. Do not invent per-step `prompt` fields; each role runs

Complexity assessment: include a `complexity` field in your

`standard` (a normal scoped task — the default), `complex`
(multi-file or multi-step investigation), or `open_ended`
(broad/unbounded; expect deep iteration). This scales the
workers' tool-call budgets up or down. Do NOT inflate it to

unattended (autonomy) task is held to a tighter ceiling
